short_description: A probabilistic study of the Yang Mills mass gap: Thorin measures, Brownian motion on SU(2) and the Migdal Kadanoff ladder, with proofs that the projected ladder contracts at every coupling and that the reciprocal heat kernel is a generalized gamma convolution. The four dimensional gap stays open.
description: The Mass Gap reads the Yang Mills mass gap problem through probability. Reflection positivity makes the spectral measure of a gauge field positive, and the book develops what that positivity buys: the gap as the exponential moment threshold of a generalized gamma convolution, and as the decay rate of its Thorin densities; Brownian motion on SU(2) and the exactly solvable theory in two dimensions; Monte Carlo estimation of the gap; and the Migdal Kadanoff renormalization ladder as a flow on laws of the plaquette. The new results are proved for the ladder, not for the four dimensional lattice. They include a product formula for the SU(2) heat kernel with monotone roots, whose reciprocal is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution; the contraction of the projected ladder at every coupling; a hypergeometric law for the coalescence of the latent count, with a harmonic law for its mean and a first rung theorem; the Thorin form of the Hartman Watson law; and the preservation of real zeros by convolution and the heat flow on SU(2). The book poses a conjecture, that link densities with real zeros beyond the edge of the group are closed under convolution, and reduces it to statements about one function at a time. Every computation is reported with its script, and theorems, leading order derivations, numerical results and open problems are kept apart. The mass gap in four dimensions is not proved here; the chapters on open problems say what is missing.

chapters.title: The Problem
chapters.summary:
This chapter states the Yang Mills mass gap problem and recasts it in the language of probability. It gives the Clay Millennium Prize formulation of Jaffe and Witten: existence of a nontrivial quantum Yang Mills theory on R^4 for a compact simple gauge group with a mass gap Delta > 0. It records the announced 2026 existence proof as a working hypothesis. Via the spectral theorem the gap becomes the left edge of the support of the spectral measure of a gauge invariant observable, so the whole problem is a question about supports of positive measures obtained as limits of lattice measures. The chapter introduces lattice gauge theory as a probability model (Haar measure, plaquette weights, Wilson loops, character expansion, transfer matrix), surveys probabilistic work on gauge theories, and gives a table of the results of the book and their status. It proves nothing new and states that no chapter proves the mass gap.

chapters.title: Positivity and the Thorin Toolkit
chapters.summary:
This chapter explains why Euclidean correlations of gauge invariant observables are Laplace transforms of nonnegative measures, and collects the tools used afterwards. Positivity comes from reflection positivity, proved for the lattice Wilson action by Osterwalder and Seiler through nonnegative character coefficients of the plaquette weight (Bochner's theorem on a compact group). Bernstein's theorem makes complete monotonicity of the correlation equivalent to a nonnegative spectral measure, whose support edge is the gap. The chapter defines the offset measure at positive Euclidean time, and proves log convexity of the correlation, monotone decrease of the effective mass to the gap (so numerical estimates only bound the gap from above), and equivalence of a gap and exponential decay. It then reviews harmonic analysis on compact groups (Peter Weyl theorem, Weyl integration and character formulas, Casimirs, Brownian motion, Jacobian of the exponential map) and the probabilistic toolkit: Stieltjes functions, generalized gamma convolutions and Thorin measures, Bondesson's shot noise representation, Levy measures, the hyperbolic laws of Biane, Pitman and Yor, likelihood ratio orders and total positivity, and positive linear inverse problems with EM deconvolution. Most of the material is classical.

- Infinite divisibility of exponential mixtures (Goldie 1967, Steutel 1967).
- Generalized gamma convolutions and Thorin measures (Thorin 1977); properties and shot noise representation (Bondesson 1992).
- Hyperbolic laws related to Brownian motion and Bessel processes (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001).
- Monotone likelihood ratio and total positivity (Karlin 1968).

chapters.title: Two Routes to the Gap
chapters.summary:
This chapter turns positivity into two translations of the mass gap into statements about generalized gamma convolutions (GGC), and tests them on solvable models. In Route A the offset spectral measure of a gauge invariant observable is itself a Thorin measure, so it defines a Yang Mills GGC, and the gap is the abscissa of exponential moments, the tail index of the GGC. In Route B the Polson 2 sin^2 lemma, from the authors' Riemann programme, transports the spectrum, regarded as a Levy measure, to a Thorin density built from a Levy exponent, namely the correlation at the offset minus the real part of the correlation continued to real time, divided by a multiple of real time. The gap is then the exact exponential decay rate of the Thorin densities in Euclidean time, with a monotone local rate. A uniform Thorin gap inequality is shown to be equivalent to a uniform spectral gap and to uniform exponential decay, with a free constant, and it passes to the continuum limit when the lattice offset measures converge weakly. A correlator with two isolated levels is not a GGC. The Ising chain with exact decimation, a massless field with power law correlations and the two dimensional Ising model (Onsager, Kaufman) illustrate a gap that survives, no gap, and a gap that closes at a critical point.

- Generalized gamma convolutions and Thorin measures (Thorin 1977); Bondesson's shot noise representation (Bondesson 1992); Kallen Lehmann spectral representation.
- Bernstein's theorem on completely monotone functions (Bernstein 1929).
- The one dimensional Ising model and its exact decimation (Ising chain, transfer matrix).
- Exact solution of the two dimensional Ising model, critical point and gap (Onsager 1944, Kaufman 1949).
- Glueball spectrum of lattice SU(3) (Morningstar and Peardon 1999); absence of a phase transition for SU(2) lattice gauge theory (Creutz 1980).

#### New results

- [The Yang Mills generalized gamma convolution of an observable](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#yang_mills_ggc) (Proposition 3.1, page 30; proved): The offset spectral measure of a gauge invariant observable is a Thorin measure, so it defines a generalized gamma convolution whose Laplace transform is built from the zero momentum propagator. - [Mass gap equals the exponential moment threshold of the Yang Mills GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#gap_as_exponential_moment_threshold) (Theorem 3.2, page 31; proved): The mass gap of an observable is the exponential rate below which the associated generalized gamma convolution has finite exponential moments and above which it does not, so the gap is a tail index. New in this book.
- [The Polson 2 sin squared lemma](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#polson_2sin2_lemma) (Lemma 3.5, page 33; proved): The compensated exponent of a single jump is a Thorin integral with an explicit nonnegative density built from a squared sine, the identity used to transport a Levy measure to a Thorin density. First stated in Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis, Volume I: Representations of Xi, Thorin Measures and the Reciprocal Xi Function, Zenodo.

New in this book.
- [Mass gap is the decay rate of the Thorin densities in Euclidean time](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#gap_as_thorin_decay_rate) (Theorem 3.7, page 35; proved): The Thorin densities decay in Euclidean time at exactly the rate given by the gap, with a monotone local rate that decreases to the gap from above. chapters.title: Estimating the Gap
chapters.summary:
This chapter treats the mass gap as a parameter to be estimated from a noisy Euclidean correlator. Recovering the spectral measure is the ill conditioned inverse Laplace transform problem (spectral reconstruction in lattice QCD), but the left edge of its support is well determined. The chapter builds a support constrained profile estimator: positive deconvolution by nonnegative least squares, a chi squared profile in the candidate gap, and a threshold rule, tested on a toy spectrum with three stable states and a two particle continuum, with a Bayesian version using a Laplace approximation and horseshoe priors. It then reviews Monte Carlo tools from Bayesian computation for lattice gauge theory: latent variable samplers, slice sampling heat bath, nested sampling and the density of states, the vertical likelihood and split sampling of Polson and Scott compared on a two dimensional SU(2) torus with exact partition function, and weighted Monte Carlo with the Yakowitz rate tested on thermodynamic integration. It can expose a wrong claim and measure a lattice gap, but cannot prove that a gap exists or reach the continuum limit.

- Backus Gilbert method (1968), maximum entropy, and smeared spectral densities for spectral reconstruction (Hansen, Lupo and Tantalo 2019).
- The EM algorithm for positive linear inverse problems (Vardi and Lee 1993), read as Monte Carlo inversion (Polson and Robert 1994); Bayesian nonparametric deconvolution (Padilla, Polson and Scott).
- Nonnegative least squares (Lawson and Hanson 1974); horseshoe priors (Carvalho, Polson and Scott 2010).
- Power posteriors (Friel and Pettitt 2008); the harmonic mean estimator (Newton and Raftery 1994); Troutt's vertical density sampler (1991); Wang and Landau sampling (2001); the 1/k ensemble (Hesselbo and Stinchcombe 1995); nested sampling (Skilling 2006).
- Vertical likelihood Monte Carlo and weighted slice sampling (Polson and Scott 2014, the first author's earlier work), which the chapter states and applies.
- Weighted Monte Carlo (Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky 1978) and its mean square error rate of order n to the minus four (Masry and Cambanis 1990).

chapters.title: Markov Chains, Mixing and Slice Variables
chapters.summary:
What limits the simulation of lattice gauge fields, and how do mixing, autocorrelation and slice variables relate to the mass gap? The chapter opens with Mark Kac: models as caricatures, Polya's recurrence theorem and marginal dimensions, Kac's lemma on mean return times, and the Feynman Kac formula linking Euclidean measures to the Hamiltonian gap. It then covers the Jerrum and Sinclair FPRAS for the ferromagnetic Ising partition function, canonical paths, the product estimator, and the relation between rapid mixing, log Sobolev constants and decay of correlations for spin systems. The Sokal section treats integrated autocorrelation time with Madras and Sokal windowing, Swendsen Wang and Edwards Sokal clusters, multigrid Monte Carlo, topological freezing in two dimensional U(1), and Lee Yang zeros. The last section covers slice variables, Higdon's partial decoupling, Besag's Markov random fields and a pseudolikelihood experiment for SU(2). It conjectures, with a sketch of proof, a log Sobolev bound for the sliced SU(2) link conditional.

chapters.title: Hitting Times and Learning the Gap
chapters.summary:
A gap is a rate; this chapter reads it in two further ways and asks how it can be learned. First, the hazard rate of a hitting time (Roberts and Shortland): standard bounds place the spectral gap of a reversible diffusion within a factor two of Dirichlet eigenvalues of sets of measure at least one half; a reflection removes the factor; Brownian motion on SU(2) hitting the equator has an exact survival law with rate 3/2; and a hazard rate estimator of the gap uses positive data. Second, moderate deviations (Rubin and Sethuraman), the Cramer series, the one loop term of the Migdal Kadanoff ladder as curvature, and, under a stated hypothesis, de Finetti's theorem as a necessary test for a unique vacuum. Third, learning: sufficient statistics of lattice gauge fields, particle learning, and generative Bayesian computation (GBC) with neural and transformer generators. Fourth, quantum Bayesian computation: the Kogut Susskind Hamiltonian of one SU(2) plaquette as a tridiagonal matrix in characters, a proof that its vacuum has only real zeros, and the limits of quantum computation. None of this proves the gap in four dimensions.

- Exponential families, Rao Blackwell, Pitman Koopman theorem, Cramer Rao bound.
- Particle learning (Carvalho, Johannes, Lopes and Polson 2010), generative Bayesian computation (Polson and Sokolov 2023) and quantum Bayesian computation (Polson, Sokolov and Xu 2023), the authors' earlier work.

chapters.title: Two Dimensions and Other Exact Models
chapters.summary:
This chapter collects the models in which the mass gap can be computed exactly, as a calibration for the four dimensional problem. The main case is two dimensional Yang Mills theory with gauge group SU(2), on the lattice and in the continuum, where the gap is a statement about Brownian motion on the three sphere: the transfer matrix is diagonal in characters, with eigenvalues given by ratios of modified Bessel functions. The chapter proves a uniform Thorin gap inequality for the two dimensional lattice theory from the coarsest lattice down to the continuum, using exact decimation and a Bessel ratio inequality. It then gives a guided tour of the method in two dimensions, an identity between Riemann's kernel for the xi function and the SU(2) sphere partition function (the return density of Brownian motion on S^3), and short sections on dynamic versus static gaps, the renormalization group for statisticians, free fields and Kallen Lehmann spectral measures, and large N with free probability (Gross Witten Wadia transition, free unitary Brownian motion).

- Continuum two dimensional Yang Mills measure (Gross, King and Sengupta 1989; Sengupta 1997; Levy 2003), and the master field (Levy 2017).
- Bessel ratio inequalities (Amos 1974).
- Riemann's cosine transform for the xi function (Riemann 1859), and the work of Polya, de Bruijn and Newman on its deformations (Polya 1926; de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976).
- Theta sum laws and the Mellin transform of xi (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001).
- The large N limit ('t Hooft 1974), hierarchical models (Dyson 1969; Bleher and Sinai 1973; Ito 1985).
- The third order large N transition (Gross and Witten 1980; Douglas and Kazakov 1993), and free unitary Brownian motion (Biane 1997).
- Equivalences between strong spatial mixing, spectral gap and log Sobolev inequality (Dobrushin and Shlosman 1985, 1987; Stroock and Zegarlinski 1992; Martinelli and Olivieri 1994), the Bakry Emery criterion (Bakry and Emery 1985), and the strong coupling dynamics of Shen, Zhu and Zhu (2023).

chapters.title: Strong Coupling and the Migdal Kadanoff Ladder
chapters.summary:
This chapter moves to four dimensional SU(2) lattice Yang Mills with the Wilson action and asks how far the gap can be controlled from strong coupling toward the continuum. It states the strong coupling character expansion and cluster expansion (the Osterwalder and Seiler theorem: a positive lattice mass and an area law), and explains why strong coupling control does not reach the continuum. It describes how glueball masses are measured by lattice Monte Carlo. It then reads the Migdal Kadanoff recursion, bond moving followed by decimation, as a Bayesian product followed by a convolution of laws, proves that each step preserves nonnegative character coefficients, so that the four dimensional lattice theory with the plaquette weight of any rung is reflection positive, and derives the coupling decrement through the mean of the Biane Pitman Yor variable, at leading order with the remainder not bounded (asymptotic freedom on the ladder). Finally it defines a heat kernel projected one dimensional map, proves its monotonicity from a monotone likelihood ratio property, and proves a first passage criterion for the correlation length. The gap criterion for the hierarchical lattice is conditional: (C) and (D) are open and (E) fails as stated, and even granted all three the remark bounds a correlation length, not the Thorin gap inequality.

#### From the literature

- Character expansion, strong coupling cluster expansion, area law and positive lattice mass for small beta (Osterwalder and Seiler 1978), with the strong coupling mass series (Munster 1981).
- The Migdal recursion (Migdal 1975) and its explanation as bond moving followed by decimation, with bond moving giving one sided bounds on the free energy (Kadanoff 1975, 1976).
- Probability laws tied to theta and zeta functions, including the variable whose Laplace transform is sqrt(2q)/sinh sqrt(2q) (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001).
- The duality between envelopes and mixtures (Polson and Scott 2016), and the Clebsch Gordan rule.
- Confinement on the Migdal Kadanoff hierarchical lattice (Ito 1985).
- Lattice Monte Carlo for glueballs (Creutz 1980; Kennedy and Pendleton 1985; Morningstar and Peardon 1999); asymptotic freedom (Gross and Wilczek 1973; Politzer 1973).

#### New results

The new statements are the positivity lemma for the ladder, the monotonicity lemma for the projected map and the first passage criterion; none of them is a proof of a gap.

chapters.title: The Ladder on Counts and Kingman's Coalescent
chapters.summary:
This chapter studies the exact Migdal Kadanoff ladder for SU(2) lattice gauge theory without the projection onto heat kernels. Heat kernels and Wilson laws are mixtures of the densities proportional to powers of one plus cosine of the angle, with a latent nonnegative integer count. Bond moving adds counts and decimation, the convolution of two such densities, thins them by an explicit positive kernel. The coalescence theorem shows this kernel is strictly positive, and the hypergeometric theorem identifies it as the law of the overlap of two random subsets, so that positivity is the Chu Vandermonde identity and the kernel is totally positive of order two. The harmonic law gives the mean count of a convolution, with the constant seven sixths, and hence the drift of minus thirteen sixteenths per rung from a point mass. The mean count is shown to be an observable, the expectation of the reciprocal of one minus cosine less two. The first rung theorem, stated on the class of laws with real zeros, gives the change of the mean count in terms of the variance to mean ratio, with explicit limits only for point masses and Wilson laws; the heat kernel value of minus one half is not proved. The second half shows that Brownian motion on SU(2) is a Wright Fisher diffusion and that heat flow is dual to the death process of Kingman's coalescent.

#### From the literature

- the coalescent (Kingman 1982) and the random walks with spherical symmetry of Kingman (1963)
- the subadditive ergodic theorem (Kingman 1973)
- the expansion of the Wright Fisher transition density in Beta laws weighted by the ancestral process (Griffiths 1980, Tavare 1984)
- exact filters for the Wright Fisher diffusion through the dual process (Chaleyat Maurel and Genon Catalot 2009, Papaspiliopoulos and Ruggiero 2014)
- total positivity of birth and death transition functions (Karlin and McGregor 1959)
- the ancestral selection graph (Krone and Neuhauser 1997)
- the Ewens sampling formula (Ewens 1972)

#### New results

The chapter's own results are the coalescence theorem, the hypergeometric kernel, the harmonic law, the first rung theorem, and the transfer of the Griffiths and Tavare duality to the SU(2) heat kernel; the open problems on log concavity and on the constant drift are also catalogued.

- [Coalescence of Beta type densities under SU(2) convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#coalescence_of_counts) (Theorem 9.1, page 139; proved): Convolving two of the basic densities proportional to powers of one plus cosine on SU(2) gives a strictly positive mixture of such densities, with a known mean count. New in this book.
- [Hypergeometric law of coalescence](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#coalescence_is_hypergeometric) (Theorem 9.4, page 141; proved): The coalescence kernel of the SU(2) convolution ladder is the hypergeometric law of the overlap of two random subsets, and its positivity is the Chu Vandermonde identity. New in this book.
- [Moments, total positivity and unnormalised form of the coalescence kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#hypergeometric_kernel_consequences) (Corollary 9.5, page 142; proved): The coalescence kernel has explicit mean and variance, is totally positive of order two, has an unnormalised closed form, and is the thinning of the entrance law of Kingman's death process. New in this book.
- [The exact Migdal Kadanoff ladder stays in the family of count mixtures](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#mixture_family_closed_under_ladder) (Corollary 9.6, page 143; proved): Heat kernels and Wilson laws on SU(2) are mixtures of the basic densities, and the family of such mixtures is closed under products and convolutions, so every rung of the exact ladder stays in it. New in this book.
- [The mean count as an expectation of a reciprocal and a character sum](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#mean_count_formula) (Corollary 9.7, page 145; proved): The mean count of a mixture equals the average of the reciprocal of one minus cosine, less two, and for the heat kernel it is twice the inverse coupling minus seven sixths to leading order. New in this book.
- [Harmonic law for the mean count of a convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#harmonic_law) (Theorem 9.8, page 147; proved): Under convolution the mean counts combine like resistances in parallel, with an explicit constant correction and an error of order one over the smallest index. New in this book.
- [Drift of the mean count from a point mass over one exact rung](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#drift_from_point_mass) (Corollary 9.9, page 148; proved): One exact rung of the ladder started from a pure power density lowers the mean count by a constant, minus thirteen sixteenths for four copies and fourfold convolution. New in this book.
- [The latent count is an observable on the group](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#count_is_an_observable) (Proposition 9.11, page 148; proved): The mean of the latent count of a link law equals the expectation of the reciprocal of the Wilson action density, less two. New in this book.
- [First rung theorem for laws with real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#first_rung_theorem) (Theorem 9.13, page 150; proved): For link laws in the class with real zeros, one exact ladder rung changes the mean count by a constant depending only on the ratio of variance to mean, with explicit limits for point masses and Wilson laws; the heat kernel value is not proved. New in this book.
- [Finite variance estimator of the count on a lattice](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#link_integrated_count_estimator) (Proposition 9.14, page 151; proved): Integrating out one link gives a bounded function of the configuration whose average is the count of a loop through that link. New in this book.
- [Laws with real zeros have a log concave count](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#real_zero_laws_log_concave_count) (Proposition 9.15, page 154; proved): The latent count law of every link density with only real zeros beyond the edge of the group is log concave. New in this book.
- [Does the exact ladder preserve log concavity of the count](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#ladder_preserves_log_concavity_problem) (Open problem 8, page 155; open): Open whether coalescence preserves log concavity of the latent count; true for laws of the real zero class, supported by exact computation otherwise. New in this book.
- [Explain the constant drift of the mean count](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#constant_drift_problem) (Open problem 9, page 155; open): Open to prove the drift of minus one half per rung for heat kernels and at later rungs; the first rung from the real zero class is proved. New in this book.
- [Brownian motion on SU(2) is a Wright Fisher diffusion](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#su2_heat_flow_is_wright_fisher) (Proposition 9.16, page 156; proved): In the variable one half of one plus cosine, the class angle of Brownian motion on SU(2) is the neutral two allele Wright Fisher diffusion with total mutation rate three, started from fixation. New in this book.
- [Kingman duality for the SU(2) heat kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#kingman_coalescent_duality) (Theorem 9.17, page 157; proved): Through the Wright Fisher form of Brownian motion on SU(2), the expansion of Griffiths and Tavare in Beta laws weighted by the ancestral process becomes an expansion of the SU(2) heat kernel in powers of one plus cosine, with Kingman's death process moving the weights. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Real Zeros
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks on what class of link laws the exact Migdal Kadanoff ladder for SU(2) acts well, and proposes a Lee Yang property: the density of a link is a product over zeros of one plus cosine of the angle divided by a number at least one, so all zeros in cosine are real and lie beyond the edge of the group. Convolution of class functions on SU(2) is written as a Hadamard product of Laurent coefficients through the circle, and Malo's theorem gives the preservation of real zeros by heat flow and by convolution when one factor has an antiderivative with real zeros and at least the same degree, so the coalescence kernel has real zeros and a Polya frequency sequence of reweighted weights. The Hartman Watson law is shown to be a generalized gamma convolution, with Thorin distribution function minus the phase of the Bessel function of imaginary order divided by pi, so the Wilson action is a Thorin mixture of heat kernels. Closure of the class under convolution, which would give a Lee Yang property for the whole ladder, is conjectured, with numerical evidence, and is left open.

#### From the literature

- the Lee Yang property for zeros of partition functions (Lee and Yang 1952)
- Malo's theorem on Hadamard products of real rooted polynomials (Malo 1895)
- the Schur Szego composition theorem (Szego 1922)
- the characterisation of Polya frequency sequences (Aissen, Schoenberg, Whitney and Edrei 1952)
- generalized gamma convolutions and Thorin measures (Thorin 1977, Bondesson 1992)
- the Hartman Watson law (Hartman and Watson 1974) and its appearance in windings of planar Brownian motion (Yor 1980)
- complete monotonicity and infinite divisibility for Bessel functions (Kent 1978, Hartman 1976)
- reality of zeros under heat flow (de Bruijn 1950); the reality of the zeros of K_{iy} in y (Polya 1926)
- Neumann's product formula and Gegenbauer's addition theorem for Bessel functions (Watson 1944)
- operators preserving real zeros (Borcea and Branden 2009; Asano 1970); the Grace, Walsh and Szego theorem (Walsh 1922, Szego 1922)

#### New results

The preservation of the class by heat flow proved here is also what Chapter 6 uses to show that the vacuum of one plaquette has real zeros.

- [Convolution on SU(2) as a Hadamard product of Laurent coefficients](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#su2_convolution_as_hadamard_product) (Lemma 10.2, page 163; proved): Convolution of class functions on SU(2) is a Hadamard product of the Laurent coefficients of one function multiplied by z minus its inverse and of an antiderivative of the other, which brings theorems on real zeros of Hadamard products to the group. New in this book.
- [Real zeros are preserved by convolution and heat flow on SU(2)](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#real_zeros_under_convolution) (Theorem 10.4, page 164; proved): Convolution of class functions on SU(2) preserves real zeros beyond the edge of the group when one factor has such an antiderivative, and heat flow preserves the class of link densities with real zeros. New in this book.
- [The coalescence has real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#coalescence_has_real_zeros) (Corollary 10.5, page 165; proved): The convolution of two basic densities is a polynomial with only real zeros beyond the edge, so its count is a sum of independent Bernoulli variables and the kernel weights form a Polya frequency sequence. New in this book.
- [Two Wilson laws convolve into the real zero class](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#wilson_times_wilson) (Proposition 10.6, page 165; proved): By Gegenbauer's addition theorem the convolution of two Wilson laws on SU(2) is a normalised Bessel function of order one, so its zeros in cosine are explicit, real and beyond the edge of the group, and its count is a sum of independent Bernoulli variables. New in this book.
- [Thorin form of the Hartman Watson law](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#thorin_form_hartman_watson) (Theorem 10.7, page 168; proved): The Hartman Watson law is a generalized gamma convolution with no drift, and its Thorin distribution function is minus the phase of the Bessel function of imaginary order divided by pi. New in this book.
- [The Wilson action is a Thorin mixture of heat kernels](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#wilson_action_thorin_mixture_of_heat_kernels) (Corollary 10.8, page 169; proved): The Wilson law on SU(2) is a mixture of heat kernels over a random time that is a generalized gamma convolution, with Thorin measure the Hartman Watson one shifted by one half. New in this book.
- [Smoothed criterion for real zeros of a convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#smoothed_criterion_real_zeros) (Theorem 10.10, page 172; proved): The convolution of two polynomial laws with real zeros has real zeros whenever one of them convolved with the basic density of the other's degree has an antiderivative with real zeros. New in this book.
- [Smoothing conjecture for real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#smoothing_conjecture) (Conjecture 10.11, page 173; open): Conjecturally, smoothing a polynomial law with real zeros by a basic density of no larger degree gives a law with a real zeroed antiderivative; it would imply closure of the class under convolution for polynomials. New in this book.
- [Radial flow identities for SU(2) convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#radial_flow_identities) (Theorem 10.12, page 174; proved): Convolution on SU(2) is a running average over the radius of convolutions on the circle of dilated laws, with explicit identities linking the two. New in this book.
- [Closure follows from the absence of a common zero along the flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#closure_from_no_common_zero) (Theorem 10.14, page 175; proved): Convolution of two polynomial laws with real zeros has real zeros if the SU(2) and circle convolutions of their dilations never share a zero. New in this book.
- [A criterion by signs for real zeros of a convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#sign_criterion_real_zeros) (Theorem 10.15, page 176; proved): Real zeros of the convolution follow if all lower convolutions have alternating signs at the zeros of the circle convolution. New in this book.
- [Interlacing conjecture for circle and SU(2) convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#interlacing_conjecture) (Conjecture 10.16, page 176; open): Conjecturally the zeros of the circle convolution strictly interlace those of the SU(2) convolution; it would imply closure of the class under convolution. New in this book.
- [Conjecture that real zero laws are closed under convolution on SU(2)](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#class_l_closed_under_convolution) (Conjecture 10.17, page 177; open): Conjecturally (supported by numerical evidence, not proved) the class of link laws with only real zeros beyond the edge of the group is closed under convolution, so the exact ladder has a Lee Yang property at every rung. New in this book.
- [A Malo type theorem for the SU(2) pairing](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#malo_type_theorem_problem) (Open problem 10, page 178; open): Open problem to prove the smoothing or interlacing conjecture, or a Malo type theorem for the pairing of the circle lemma when neither factor has an antiderivative in the class. New in this book.

#### Key terms

real zeros, Lee Yang property, Malo's theorem, Hadamard product, Polya frequency sequence, Schur Szego composition, generalized gamma convolution, Thorin measure, Hartman Watson law, heat flow, class L, closure under convolution

chapters.title: Theta Kernels, Fermion Determinants and Howe Duality
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks which parts of a chain of theta lifts, used in an argument for the Riemann hypothesis announced in 2026 and read here through unpublished accounts, have a counterpart for lattice Yang Mills with gauge group SU(2); it gives no verdict on that argument. Plaquette laws with real zeros in the cosine of the angle (the Thorin class) are shown to be products of fermion determinants det(1+alpha U) with real hopping parameters, and their characters are theta lifts in the sense of Howe duality, given by Schur functions of the flavour group. Decimation, the convolution of two such laws, has an exact expansion over matchings of the complete graph on the flavours, which places the open closure conjecture for laws with real zeros next to the Heilmann and Lieb theorem. Three mechanisms of the expanded account that contain no number theory are translated: a one sided window criterion, which for a positive spectral measure becomes an elementary proposition with a monotone upper bound estimator of the gap built on negative binomial weights (a lattice Post and Widder kernel); a positive selector over channels; and an approximate tight frame lemma, given in a sharp form, which bounds averages such as string tensions and not gaps. The chapter ends with an inequality of type (M) for the renormalization ladder and open problems.

#### From the literature

- Howe duality and the dual Cauchy identity for the pair of general linear groups (Howe 1989).
- The matching polynomial has only real zeros (Heilmann and Lieb 1972).
- The colour flavour transformation (Zirnbauer 1996) and its use for an induced lattice U(N) gauge theory (Budczies and Zirnbauer 2003).
- The Jacobi triple product, read as a free fermion.
- The inversion formula with gamma kernels (Post 1930, Widder 1941).
- The Harder and Narasimhan filtration (Harder and Narasimhan 1975), mentioned for the slope.
- The frame lemma, and its passage from a count to a mean, from an unpublished exposition written at the behest of M. O. Rubinstein (2026).

#### New results

Only the statements about Yang Mills below are the authors' own.

- [Laws with real zeros are products of SU(2) fermion determinants](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#laws_with_real_zeros_are_determinants) (Proposition 11.1, page 180; proved): A plaquette law of the real zero class is a product of one flavour fermion determinants with real hopping parameters. New in this book.
- [Characters of a determinant law from the flavour group (Howe duality)](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#characters_from_flavour_group) (Proposition 11.2, page 181; proved): The character coefficients of a product of fermion determinants are positive combinations of Schur functions of the hopping parameters. New in this book.
- [Convolution of class functions on SU(2) as an average over an ellipse](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#convolution_ellipse_average) (Lemma 11.3, page 182; proved): The convolution of two class functions on SU(2) at cos theta equal to x is an area average over an ellipse in the plane of two cosines. New in this book.
- [Matching expansion for the convolution of determinant laws](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#matching_expansion_of_decimation) (Theorem 11.4, page 182; proved): The convolution of two products of fermion determinants on SU(2) is an explicit sum over matchings of the flavours, a new exact formula for decimation. New in this book.
- [One sided windows and a monotone upper bound estimator for the gap](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#windows_for_the_gap) (Proposition 11.5, page 185; proved): Adapting the window criterion of an unpublished account of the Riemann hypothesis argument, for a positive spectral measure a decay bound on a sparse set of times bounds the gap, and a negative binomial estimator gives monotone rigorous upper bounds. New in this book.
- [A sharp form of the frame lemma from an exposition of the Alpoge argument](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#frame_lemma_sharp_form) (Proposition 11.7, page 187; proved): A sharpened constant in the frame lemma for sums of images of subspaces, attained for tight frames of isometries. New in this book.
- [An inequality of type (M) for the Migdal Kadanoff ladder](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_type_m_inequality_for_ladder) (Open problem 11, page 191; open): Show that the exact blocked plaquette count stays below the ladder count plus a small error, until strong coupling is reached. New in this book.
- [Colour flavour transformation for SU(2) as a symplectic group](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_symplectic_colour_flavour) (Open problem 13, page 193; open): Carry out the colour flavour transformation for SU(2) with its inner pairs and identify the mixing law. New in this book.
- [Bound the error per rung of the ladder below the drift](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_slopes_error_per_rung) (Open problem 14, page 193; open): Bound the error per blocking step below the drift one half of the count, which with a bound on the first error would give the type (M) inequality. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: A Path to the Mass Gap
chapters.summary:
This chapter assembles the results of the book into a programme for the mass gap of four dimensional SU(2) lattice Yang Mills. It lists five stages: positivity at every scale (reflection positivity, nonnegative character coefficients), strong coupling (cluster expansion), the Migdal Kadanoff renormalization ladder, the comparison of the true block spin flow on the lattice Z^4 with Migdal Kadanoff type flows (open, and the place where a new idea is needed), and the continuum theory. It explains why the bracketing arguments of Kadanoff and Tomboulis do not control spectral measures, poses the comparison as a Thorin sandwich between two Migdal Kadanoff type maps in the likelihood ratio order, and collects open problems: an explicit remainder in the decrement, the likelihood ratio property and monotonicity for SU(3), the next order of the decrement against the two loop beta function, a Bayesian gap estimator for glueball correlators, and the uniform Thorin gap inequality at strong coupling with explicit constants. It weighs three routes to the missing step, discusses recent work of others and unused ideas (centre vortices, monopoles, gradient flow, resurgence, holography, Hamiltonian lattice formulations, formal verification, loop equations, generalised symmetries), and argues for attempting three dimensional SU(2) first, where the flow is superrenormalizable, with the open problem of a mass gap of at least c_0 over beta at every coupling.

#### From the literature

- Bond moving inequalities (Kadanoff 1975, 1976) and the Migdal recursion (Migdal 1975).
- Confinement on Migdal Kadanoff hierarchical lattices (Ito 1985).
- A claimed confinement proof by bracketing (Tomboulis 2007) and its critique (Ito and Seiler 2007, 2008).
- The strong coupling cluster expansion (Osterwalder and Seiler 1978) and the stochastic analysis approach (Shen, Zhu and Zhu 2023).
- Ultraviolet control by the renormalization group (Balaban 1987) and finite volume SU(2) Yang Mills (Magnen, Rivasseau and Seneor 1993).
- The three dimensional vacuum wavefunction and string tension (Karabali, Kim and Nair 1998) and lattice data (Teper 1999).

#### New results

Open problems of the list are catalogued below, except the restated Thorin sandwich and the next order of the decrement, answered in Chapter 13.

- [Thorin sandwich for the four dimensional flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#thorin_sandwich) (Open problem 15, page 197; open): Find two Migdal Kadanoff type maps whose flows bracket the true spectral measures, with a decrement inequality for the lower one. New in this book.
- [Explicit remainder for the decrement of the Migdal Kadanoff ladder](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_explicit_decrement_remainder) (Open problem 16, page 200; open): Bound explicitly the first correction to the leading decrement of the four dimensional SU(2) Migdal Kadanoff ladder, using the variance of the Biane, Pitman and Yor variable. New in this book.
- [Likelihood ratio property and monotonicity of the ladder for SU(3)](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_likelihood_ratio_su3) (Open problem 17, page 200; open): Prove the monotone likelihood ratio in time of the heat kernel analytically and extend the monotonicity and covering arguments of the ladder to SU(3); the SU(2) half is solved in Chapter 13. New in this book.
- [Bayesian gap estimator for lattice glueball correlators](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_glueball_gap_estimator) (Open problem 19, page 200; open): Apply the book's Bayesian estimator of the mass gap to published lattice glueball correlators and test the Migdal Kadanoff ladder against them at intermediate couplings. New in this book.
- [Uniform Thorin gap inequality at strong coupling with explicit constants](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_strong_coupling_thorin_gap) (Open problem 20, page 200; open): Prove from the cluster expansion, with explicit constants, the uniform decay inequality for Thorin densities that is equivalent to a uniform spectral gap, and push it toward the crossover. New in this book.
- [Mass gap of order one over beta for three dimensional SU(2) by bracketing](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_three_dimensional_gap) (Open problem 22, page 212; open): Prove a mass gap at least a constant over beta for three dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory at every coupling, by bracketing one block spin step between two contracting Migdal Kadanoff maps. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Progress on the Open Problems
chapters.summary:
This chapter reports the authors' progress on the open problems of the programme for the SU(2) Migdal Kadanoff renormalization ladder. The SU(2) heat kernel is a product of linear factors in the cosine of the angle (a Laguerre Polya class function) whose roots gamma_m(t) exceed one and move monotonically in time, and its reciprocal has a Thorin form with atoms at these roots. Hence the heat kernel has strict monotone likelihood ratio in time at every time and is strictly log concave in the cosine, and the projected map is monotone. Further results: an elementary large time bound; monotone likelihood ratio of the heat flow of the Wilson law exactly for kappa at most three halves; the weak coupling expansion of the ladder decrement for SU(2), and its first two orders for SU(N); a local heat kernel time; and total positivity of order two of convolution, proved for bond moved laws on the near hemisphere and failing, numerically, in a small cap at the antipode. The projected ladder contracts at every coupling: the time scaled score t d log K_t/dx decreases in t, by Hamilton's matrix Harnack inequality and an explicit small time analysis, so R(beta) is below beta for every beta and scale factor in four dimensions. Existence of the ladder string tension is proved under stated hypotheses and tested against lattice data; the exact ladder and the true lattice flow remain open.

#### From the literature

- The Laguerre Polya class and multiplier sequences (Polya and Schur 1914), and the Polya class of the Riemann Xi function (Polya 1926).
- Monotone motion of zeros under the heat flow (de Bruijn 1950, Newman 1976).
- Total positivity of one dimensional diffusions (Karlin and McGregor 1959).
- The matrix Harnack inequality for the heat equation (Hamilton 1993).
- The Wilson action (Wilson 1974), the effective coupling (Parisi 1980), the Migdal Kadanoff recursion (Migdal 1975, Kadanoff 1976), lattice string tension data (Teper 1998, 1999) and the Biane, Pitman and Yor law (2001).

#### New results

The headline results are the product formula and the contraction of the projected ladder.

- [Product formula for the SU(2) heat kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#product_formula) (Theorem 13.1, page 213; proved): The SU(2) heat kernel is a product of linear factors in cos theta whose real roots all lie beyond the edge of the group and move monotonically in time. New in this book.
- [Monotone likelihood ratio in time for the SU(2) heat kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#likelihood_ratio_property) (Corollary 13.2, page 214; proved): The SU(2) heat kernel has strictly monotone likelihood ratio in time at every time, so the projected Migdal Kadanoff map is increasing at every coupling. New in this book.
- [Strict log concavity of the SU(2) heat kernel and its powers in cos theta](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#heat_kernel_log_concavity) (Corollary 13.3, page 214; proved): The heat kernel, and every plaquette law made from it by bond moving, is strictly log concave as a function of the cosine of the angle. New in this book.
- [Thorin form of the SU(2) heat kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#heat_kernel_thorin_form) (Corollary 13.4, page 214; proved): The reciprocal of the SU(2) heat kernel, as a function of the cosine of the angle, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution with unit atoms at the roots of the product formula. New in this book.

chapters.title: Inequalities Between the Ladder and the Lattice
chapters.summary:
This chapter compares the Migdal Kadanoff ladder with the true four dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory, the comparison that step 4 of the book's path to the mass gap needs. It tests the sandwich idea on one block spin step of scale factor two: the law of a blocked plaquette, the 2x2 Wilson loop holonomy, is measured by heat bath Monte Carlo on an 8^4 lattice at six couplings and compared with an independent plaquette caricature and with the Migdal Kadanoff bond moving caricature, in mean and in the likelihood ratio order. The measured law lies between them in mean at every coupling and in likelihood ratio order on most of the mass. The chapter then treats correlation inequalities: Griffiths and Ginibre inequalities for abelian models, a doubling inequality derived from reflection positivity and the Schwarz inequality that proves W22 >= W12^2 >= W11^4 for every compact gauge group, a rigorous heat bath (multihit, Rao Blackwell) upper bound for SU(2) loops, and Kadanoff's variational upper bound on the pressure that holds along the whole ladder. It reports a first empirical rung with pseudolikelihood fits of the blocked coupling, states a weak coupling sandwich conjecture, and lists what a proof of the Migdal Kadanoff end would need.

#### From the literature

Griffiths' inequalities for Ising ferromagnets (Griffiths 1967); the general formulation of Griffiths inequalities (Ginibre 1970); the FKG inequality (Fortuin, Kasteleyn and Ginibre 1971); reflection positivity of the Wilson lattice measure and the loop inequalities it gives, among them W22 >= W12^2 >= W11^4 for every compact group (Osterwalder and Seiler 1978); convexity of the static quark potential from reflection positivity (Bachas 1986); the multihit estimator for Wilson loops and the perimeter bound it gives (Parisi, Petronzio and Rapuano 1983) and Rao Blackwellisation (Blackwell 1947); Migdal's and Kadanoff's recursions (Migdal 1975, Kadanoff 1975 and 1976); Kadanoff's variational bound on the pressure by bond moving; Monte Carlo renormalization group (Swendsen 1979).

#### New results

Only the weak coupling sandwich conjecture is the authors' own; the other labelled statements of the chapter are known results presented in the book's form.

- [Weak coupling sandwich for the 2x2 and 4x4 Wilson loops](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#weak_coupling_sandwich_conjecture) (Conjecture 14.1, page 243; open): The book conjectures that at weak coupling the logarithms of the 2x2 and 4x4 Wilson loops lie strictly between the independent plaquette value and the Migdal Kadanoff value, a statement supported by four numerical cases and not proved. New in this book.
- [Likelihood ratio sandwich for the 2x2 Wilson loop](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_likelihood_ratio_sandwich_2x2) (Open problem 23, page 245; open): Prove that the law of the 2x2 loop holonomy dominates the Migdal Kadanoff law built from the plaquette law in the likelihood ratio order, and that both ends of the sandwich hold in that order. New in this book.
- [Bare Migdal Kadanoff end of the Wilson loop sandwich](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_bare_migdal_kadanoff_end) (Open problem 24, page 251; open): Prove that the expectation of the 2x2 Wilson loop in SU(2) lattice gauge theory is at most the fourth power of a Bessel ratio at the bond moving coupling, in every dimension and at every coupling. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Neighbouring Problems
chapters.summary:
This chapter collects problems next to the mass gap that share its mathematics. It begins with the Lee and Yang circle theorem, Polya's Hilfssatz II and Kac's equal coupling proof, puts them in Thorin form by a Frullani bridge, and applies the method to the smallest Yang Mills systems: one plaquette, whose reciprocal partition function is the Laplace transform of a Brownian hitting time of the sphere S^3 with Fisher zeros at Bessel zeros, and a two dimensional heat kernel torus whose partition function zeros lie on fixed rays. The second section reads stochastic quantisation, the lattice Langevin equation and nonlinear filtering (Zakai and Kushner Stratonovich equations) alongside the Migdal Kadanoff ladder, and proves a continuous scale form of the projected ladder with a beta function given by a covariance. The third reads the authors' Hilbert sixth problem book for Feynman Kac, Nelson's stochastic mechanics and Levy area derivations of the gap and of the coefficient 11/3. The last sections take from the Riemann and Langlands books the Sato Tate law as Haar measure on SU(2), Ramanujan graphs, passage times on representations, a latent count for the heat kernel, and a limitation theorem.

#### From the literature

The Lee and Yang circle theorem (Lee and Yang 1952); Polya's Hilfssatz II (Polya 1926); Kac's equal coupling proof (Kac 1974); generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977, Bondesson 1992); Bessel hitting times (Ciesielski and Taylor 1962, Kent 1978); stochastic quantisation of Yang Mills (Parisi and Wu 1981; Chandra, Chevyrev, Hairer and Shen 2022); Nelson's stochastic mechanics (Nelson 1966); Greensite's vacuum wave functional conjecture (Greensite 1979); Kesten and McKay laws for regular graphs (Kesten 1959, McKay 1981); the Alon Boppana bound (Alon 1986); Ramanujan graphs (Lubotzky, Phillips and Sarnak 1988); Deligne's theorem (Deligne 1974); Selberg's eigenvalue bound (Selberg 1965; Kim and Sarnak 2003); Keilson's passage time theorem (Keilson 1979); Polya Gamma augmentation (Polson, Scott and Windle 2013); the ground state representation (Nelson 1973, Gross 1975).

#### New results

- [Frullani bridge between Lee Yang zeros and Thorin form](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#frullani_bridge) (Theorem 15.1, page 259; proved): For an even entire function of order one, real zeros are equivalent to Polya's operator preserving real zeros and to the reciprocal of its rotated form being the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution. First stated in Polson (2026), From Polya's Hilfssatz II to the Thorin representation: a probabilistic synthesis, manuscript.
- [One plaquette partition function as a Brownian hitting time](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#plaquette_hitting_time) (Proposition 15.2, page 260; proved): The reciprocal of the one plaquette SU(2) partition function in the squared coupling is the Laplace transform of the time Brownian motion in four dimensions takes to reach the unit sphere, a generalized gamma convolution with Thorin atoms at the Bessel zeros. New in this book.
- [Zeros of the heat kernel torus partition function on fixed rays](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#zeros_on_fixed_rays) (Theorem 15.3, page 261; proved): For two dimensional SU(2) with the heat kernel action on a torus, the zeros in complex time lie on the same rays for every area, determined by the zeros of one theta type series, which has none in the disc of radius 0.83; the width of the zero free sector is only computed. New in this book.
- [Zero free sector for the Wilson action on tori and hierarchical lattices](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_zero_free_sector_tori) (Open problem 25, page 262; open): Prove a zero free sector around the positive coupling axis, uniform in the volume, for two dimensional tori and for hierarchical lattices. New in this book.
- [The projected Migdal Kadanoff ladder in continuous scale](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#projected_ladder_continuous_scale) (Proposition 15.4, page 267; proved): In continuous scale the Migdal Kadanoff ladder projected on the SU(2) heat kernel has a beta function given by a covariance, which is positive at every coupling. New in this book.
- [Why the ladder decrement reproduces the background field coefficient](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#op_decrement_four_minus_third) (Open problem 26, page 270; open): Explain why the Migdal Kadanoff decrement built from the mean one third reproduces, at scale factor two, a coefficient that the background field computation writes as four minus one third. New in this book.
- [Passage times of the walk on SU(2) representations](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#passage_times_on_representations) (Proposition 15.6, page 275; proved): The first passage time to the representation of dimension N for the continuous time walk on the representations of SU(2) is a generalized gamma convolution with explicit atoms and mean (N^2-1)/3. New in this book.
- [Latent count representation of the SU(2) heat kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#latent_count_heat_kernel) (Proposition 15.7, page 276; proved): The SU(2) heat kernel is a mixture of powers of one plus cosine with a sum of independent Bernoulli variables as exponent, so that given a latent count the half angle cosine squared is Beta distributed. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: The Programme, the History and the Results
chapters.summary:
This closing chapter has three parts. First, a research programme of twelve numbered problems (with a problem 1a), ordered by estimated difficulty from certifying the Migdal Kadanoff ladder on hierarchical lattices, through string tension on hierarchical lattices, the likelihood ratio property for SU(3) and Griffiths type inequalities for SU(2), to the mass gap in three dimensions and the Clay Millennium problem in four. Second, historical notes on gauge theory from Weyl and Yang and Mills to Wilson's lattice formulation, constructive field theory from the Osterwalder Schrader axioms and Balaban's renormalization group work, hierarchical lattice confinement and the Tomboulis proposal, infinitely divisible laws and generalized gamma convolutions, and Monte Carlo and Markov random fields, together with a record of the 26 October 2026 announcement by OpenAI of an existence proof for four dimensional Yang Mills, endorsed by a review group chaired by David Gross but not refereed, disputed in public, and claiming neither confinement nor a mass gap; the authors have not checked it. Third, a summary of the results of the book with their status and home chapters, the computational findings, a scorecard of the ladder against lattice data, and the conjectures and open problems that remain.

#### From the literature

Weyl's gauge principle (1918, 1929); the Yang Mills equations (Yang and Mills 1954); Faddeev and Popov quantisation (1967); renormalizability ('t Hooft 1971, 't Hooft and Veltman 1972); asymptotic freedom (Gross and Wilczek 1973, Politzer 1973); the Wilson lattice formulation (Wilson 1974); Creutz's SU(2) simulations (1980); the Osterwalder Schrader axioms (1973, 1975); Osterwalder and Seiler's reflection positivity and strong coupling gap (1978); Luscher's transfer matrix (1977); exact two dimensional Yang Mills (Migdal 1975, Gross, King and Sengupta 1989, Driver 1989, Witten 1991); Balaban's renormalization group analysis (1983 to 1989); Migdal Kadanoff recursions (1975, 1976) and Ito's confinement on hierarchical lattices (1985); Tomboulis's bracketing proposal (2007) and the Ito and Seiler critique; Thorin (1977) and Bondesson on generalized gamma convolutions; Biane, Pitman and Yor (2001); Andrews and Mallows (1974); Kennedy and Pendleton (1985); Swendsen and Wang (1987); Edwards and Sokal (1988); Besag (1974, 1975); Jerrum and Sinclair (1993); Newman (1976).

results.name: The Yang Mills generalized gamma convolution of an observable
results.summary: The offset spectral measure of a gauge invariant observable is a Thorin measure, so it defines a generalized gamma convolution whose Laplace transform is built from the zero momentum propagator.
results.statement: Fix a gauge invariant observable with spectral measure \mu, gap \Delta=\inf\operatorname{supp}\mu>0, an offset \alpha>\alpha_0 with offset measure \mu_\alpha(dE)=e^{-\alpha E}\mu(dE), and offset correlation C(\alpha+r)=\int e^{-rE}\mu_\alpha(dE). Let \widehat C_\alpha(s)=\int_0^\infty e^{-sr}C(\alpha+r)\,dr=\int \mu_\alpha(dE)/(s+E). Then \varphi_\alpha(s)=\exp\big(-\int_0^s\widehat C_\alpha(r)\,dr\big)=\exp\big(-\int\log(1+s/E)\,\mu_\alpha(dE)\big) is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution X_\alpha whose Thorin measure is \mu_\alpha.
results.label: prop:ymggc

results.name: Mass gap equals the exponential moment threshold of the Yang Mills GGC
results.summary: The mass gap of an observable is the exponential rate below which the associated generalized gamma convolution has finite exponential moments and above which it does not, so the gap is a tail index.
results.statement: With X_\alpha the Yang Mills generalized gamma convolution of an observable with spectral measure \mu, offset \alpha>\alpha_0 and gap \Delta=\inf\operatorname{supp}\mu>0, \mathbb{E}\, e^{\lambda X_\alpha}<\infty for \lambda<\Delta and \mathbb{E}\, e^{\lambda X_\alpha}=\infty for \lambda>\Delta. Equivalently, the abscissa of convergence of the Laplace transform \varphi_\alpha is -\Delta, and the left edge of the Thorin support is the gap.
results.label: thm:abscissaB

results.name: The Polson 2 sin squared lemma
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis, Volume I: Representations of Xi, Thorin Measures and the Reciprocal Xi Function, Zenodo.
results.summary: The compensated exponent of a single jump is a Thorin integral with an explicit nonnegative density built from a squared sine, the identity used to transport a Levy measure to a Thorin density.
results.statement: For x>0, w>0 and u=w^2/2, e^{-wx}+wx-1=\int_0^\infty \log\big(1+\tfrac{u}{z}\big)\,k_x(z)\,dz, where k_x(z)=\frac{x}{\pi\sqrt{2z}}\,2\sin^2\big(x\sqrt{z/2}\big)\ge 0.
results.label: lem:2sin2B

results.name: The Thorin density is a Levy exponent
results.summary: The Thorin density obtained by transporting the spectrum is a Levy exponent divided by a multiple of real time: the exponent of a symmetric compound Poisson process, equal to the correlation at the offset minus the real part of the correlation continued to real time.
results.statement: Let \mu be a nonnegative spectral measure with offset measure \mu_\alpha(dE)=e^{-\alpha E}\mu(dE), \alpha>\alpha_0, correlation C, and L_\alpha(w)=\int_0^w (C(\alpha)-C(\alpha+s))\,ds=\int (e^{-wE}+wE-1)\,\mu_\alpha(dE)/E. Then u\mapsto\exp(-L_\alpha(\sqrt{2u})) is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has density T_\alpha(z)=\psi_\alpha(t)/(\pi t) with t=\sqrt{2z}, where \psi_\alpha(t)=\int(1-\cos tE)\,\mu_\alpha(dE)=C(\alpha)-\operatorname{Re}C(\alpha+it). Here \psi_\alpha is the Levy exponent of the symmetric compound Poisson process whose jump measure is \mu_\alpha symmetrised (jumps \pm E, each with weight \tfrac12\mu_\alpha(dE)).
results.label: thm:thorinB

results.name: Mass gap is the decay rate of the Thorin densities in Euclidean time
results.summary: The Thorin densities decay in Euclidean time at exactly the rate given by the gap, with a monotone local rate that decreases to the gap from above.
results.statement: Let \mu be the spectral measure of a gauge invariant observable, \Delta=\inf\operatorname{supp}\mu, and T_\alpha(z) the Thorin density of the previous theorem at offset \alpha>\alpha_0. (i) For all z>0 and \alpha\ge\alpha'>\alpha_0, T_\alpha(z)\le e^{-\Delta(\alpha-\alpha')}T_{\alpha'}(z). (ii) For all but countably many z, \lim_{\alpha\to\infty}-\alpha^{-1}\log T_\alpha(z)=\Delta. (iii) For each z with T_\alpha(z)>0, \alpha\mapsto\log T_\alpha(z) is convex, so the local rate r_\alpha(z)=-\partial_\alpha\log T_\alpha(z) is nonincreasing, and for z outside the exceptional countable set of (ii) it decreases to \Delta.
results.label: thm:rateB

results.name: Uniform Thorin gap inequality is equivalent to a uniform spectral gap, with constant one
results.summary: A uniform inequality between Thorin densities at different Euclidean times is equivalent to a uniform spectral gap and to uniform exponential decay, and its constant can always be taken to be one.
results.statement: Let {\mu^{(a)}} be nonnegative measures on (0,\infty) with \sup_a\int e^{-\alpha_0E}\mu^{(a)}(dE)<\infty, let C^{(a)} and T^{(a)}_\alpha be the correlations and Thorin densities of \mu^{(a)}, and let m>0. The following are equivalent. (a) \operatorname{supp}\mu^{(a)}\subset[m,\infty) for every a. (b) There are M' and \tau_0 with C^{(a)}(\tau)\le M'e^{-m\tau} for all \tau\ge\tau_0 and all a. (c) There is M<\infty with T^{(a)}_\alpha(z)\le M e^{-m(\alpha-\alpha')}T^{(a)}_{\alpha'}(z) for all a, all z and all \alpha\ge\alpha'>\alpha_0. (d) Statement (c) holds with M=1.
results.label: thm:equivB

results.name: A uniform Thorin gap inequality gives a gap in the continuum limit
results.summary: If lattice offset measures converge weakly and satisfy the uniform Thorin gap inequality with one rate, the continuum theory has a gap at least that rate.
results.statement: For lattice spacings a>0 let \mu^{(a)} be nonnegative lattice spectral measures on (0,\infty) in physical units, with \sup_a\int e^{-\alpha_0E}\mu^{(a)}(dE)<\infty, whose offset measures e^{-\alpha_0E}\mu^{(a)}(dE) converge weakly as a\to0 to e^{-\alpha_0E}\mu(dE), where \mu is the spectral measure of the continuum theory. For \alpha>\alpha_0 and z>0 let T^{(a)}_\alpha(z)=\frac{1}{\pi t}\int(1-\cos tE)\,e^{-\alpha E}\mu^{(a)}(dE), with t=\sqrt{2z}, be the Thorin densities. If there are \Delta_0>0 and M<\infty with T^{(a)}_\alpha(z)\le M e^{-\Delta_0(\alpha-\alpha')}T^{(a)}_{\alpha'}(z) for all a, all z>0 and all \alpha\ge\alpha'>\alpha_0 (the uniform Thorin gap inequality), then \inf\operatorname{supp}\mu\ge\Delta_0, that is, the continuum theory has a gap of at least \Delta_0.
results.label: cor:continuumB

results.name: A correlator with two isolated levels is not a GGC
results.summary: When the spectrum has two isolated levels, the normalised correlation in Euclidean time is not a generalized gamma convolution and not hyperbolically completely monotone.
results.statement: If \int_0^\infty C(\alpha+s)\,ds<\infty and the spectral measure \mu has atoms at E_1<E_2 with \mu((E_1,E_2))=0, then the probability density proportional to C(\alpha+\tau) in \tau is not a generalized gamma convolution, and hence not hyperbolically completely monotone.
results.label: prop:notggcB

results.name: An FPRAS for the partition function of SU(2) lattice gauge theory
results.summary: The book asks whether the partition function of SU(2) lattice gauge theory with the Wilson action can be approximated in time polynomial in the box size at every coupling.
results.statement: Is there a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for the partition function of SU(2) lattice gauge theory with the Wilson action, on boxes of side L, at every coupling, with running time polynomial in L?
results.label: op:mixing1

results.name: Slice variables give log concave conditionals
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (1996), Convergence of Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms, in Bayesian Statistics 5, Oxford University Press.
results.summary: Slicing each quasi concave likelihood factor makes the conditional law of the parameter log concave, even when the posterior itself is multimodal.
results.statement: Let the target be proportional to p(x) times the product over i=1,...,m of L_i(x) on R^d, with slice variables w=(w_1,...,w_m) and joint density proportional to p(x) times the product of the indicators I{0<w_i<L_i(x)}. If p is log concave and every L_i is quasi concave, meaning that its superlevel sets are convex, then for every w the conditional law of x given w is log concave.
results.label: prop:slicelc

results.name: Log Sobolev bound for the sliced SU(2) link conditional
results.summary: The book conjectures that, once the plaquette slices are cut at positive levels, the uniform law on the resulting intersection of spherical caps in SU(2) has a log Sobolev constant that does not depend on the coupling or the staples (a proof is only sketched).
results.statement: Identify SU(2) with the unit sphere S^3. For a link U with staples V_p, p running over the plaquettes containing U, and slice levels c_p, let C(w) be the intersection over p of the caps {U : (1/2) tr(U V_p) > c_p}. Conjecture: if every slice level satisfies c_p > 0, then C(w) is geodesically convex, and the uniform law on C(w), with the reflected Brownian motion on it, satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant 2, independent of beta and of the staples.
results.label: prop:slicecurv

results.name: Gap of the odd sector as a Dirichlet eigenvalue
results.summary: When a measure preserving reflection splits the state space into two halves, the lowest odd eigenvalue is the Dirichlet eigenvalue of the fixed set, which removes the factor of two in the hitting time bracket.
results.statement: For a reversible diffusion with generator L, invariant probability mu and spectral gap lambda_1 (the bottom of the spectrum of -L on functions of mean zero), let rho be an involution of the state space that preserves mu and commutes with L, and suppose that the complement of its fixed set F has exactly two components, each connected and exchanged by rho, so that every continuous path from a point to its image meets F. Then the lowest eigenvalue of -L on functions odd under rho equals lambda_D(F), the bottom of the spectrum of -L with Dirichlet condition on F. In particular lambda_1 <= lambda_D(F), with equality when the first excited state is odd.
results.label: prop:hitreflect

results.name: Exact survival law of Brownian motion on SU(2) hitting the equator
results.summary: The survival probability of Brownian motion on SU(2) until it reaches the equator is an explicit series whose hazard rate tends to the spectral gap 3/2.
results.statement: Let Brownian motion on SU(2)=S^3 have generator (1/2) times the Laplace Beltrami operator of the unit sphere, start at the identity, and let T be its first hitting time of the equator {a_0=0}, where a_0 is the real part of the group element. Then P(T>t) = (16/pi) times the sum over k>=1 of (-1)^(k+1) k^2/(4k^2-1) times exp(-(4k^2-1)t/2). So the hazard rate of T tends to 3/2, the spectral gap of this Brownian motion, with the next correction of relative size e^{-6t}.
results.label: prop:equator

results.name: Gap of the one plaquette SU(2) Hamiltonian
results.summary: The single plaquette Kogut Susskind Hamiltonian is a tridiagonal matrix in the character basis, with gap 3 lambda/4 at strong coupling and tending to the square root of 2 at weak coupling.
results.statement: Consider the Hamiltonian H_lambda = -lambda Delta + (1/lambda)(1 - cos theta) of one SU(2) plaquette on class functions, where Delta is the Laplacian whose eigenvalue on the character chi_n is -(n^2-1)/4 and lambda>0 is proportional to the square of the coupling. In the orthonormal basis chi_1, chi_2, ... of class functions, H_lambda is the tridiagonal matrix with diagonal entries (1/4) lambda (n^2-1) + 1/lambda and off diagonal entries -1/(2 lambda). Its gap is (3/4) lambda + O(1/lambda^3) as lambda tends to infinity and tends to sqrt(2) as lambda tends to 0.
results.label: prop:oneplaquette

results.name: The vacuum of one plaquette has real zeros
results.summary: The ground state of the one plaquette Hamiltonian, as a function of the cosine of the angle, has only real zeros at or below minus one, so its reciprocal is a Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (Thorin form).
results.statement: Let H_lambda = -lambda Delta + (1/lambda)(1 - cos theta), with lambda > 0, be the Kogut Susskind Hamiltonian of one SU(2) plaquette on class functions, where e^{\pm i theta} are the eigenvalues of the plaquette variable and Delta is the Laplacian whose eigenvalue on the character chi_n is -(n^2-1)/4. The ground state psi_0 of H_lambda, as an entire function of x = cos(theta), has only real zeros, all in (-infinity,-1]. Hence psi_0(x) = psi_0(0) e^{ax} times the product over m of (1 + x/gamma_m), with a >= 0 and gamma_m >= 1, and psi_0(0)/psi_0(x) is the Laplace transform in x of a generalized gamma convolution with drift a and unit Thorin atoms at the gamma_m. The same holds for the vacuum density psi_0^2, with atoms of weight two.
results.label: prop:vacuumzeros

results.name: Log concave count law of the one plaquette vacuum
results.summary: The vacuum density of one plaquette is a mixture of the count densities with a log concave mixing law whose mean is the count reported in the book's table.
results.statement: Let H_lambda = -lambda Delta + (1/lambda)(1 - cos theta), with lambda > 0, be the Hamiltonian of one SU(2) plaquette on class functions (Delta the Laplacian with eigenvalue -(n^2-1)/4 on the character chi_n), and psi_0 its ground state. The vacuum density psi_0^2 is a mixture, the sum over j of pi(j) f_j, with a log concave count law pi, where f_j is the density on SU(2) for which cos^2(theta/2) has the Beta(j+3/2, 3/2) law. The mean of pi is the count E[1/(1-cos theta)] - 2 of the density psi_0^2.
results.label: cor:vacuumcount

results.name: Real zeros of the vacuum of two plaquettes sharing a link
results.summary: Open whether the vacuum of two SU(2) plaquettes sharing a link, as a function of each plaquette variable, again has only real zeros below minus one.
results.statement: Two plaquettes sharing a link, in the Hamiltonian formulation and restricted to gauge invariant states. Is the vacuum, as a function of each plaquette variable cos(theta_p) with the other held fixed, an entire function with only real zeros below -1? This is the Hamiltonian form of the conjecture that the class L of laws of real zero type is closed under convolution on SU(2); the difficulty is that the heat flow on the shared link acts on both variables at once.
results.label: op:twoplaquettes

results.name: Register rule for the one plaquette gap
results.summary: Open whether the number of characters needed for the one plaquette gap grows like the square root of the vacuum count as the coupling goes to zero.
results.statement: Let H_lambda = -lambda Delta + (1/lambda)(1 - cos theta), with lambda > 0, be the Hamiltonian of one SU(2) plaquette on class functions (Delta the Laplacian with eigenvalue -(n^2-1)/4 on the character chi_n), with ground state psi_0. Prove that the number of characters needed to compute the gap of H_lambda to a fixed accuracy is asymptotic, as lambda tends to 0, to a constant times the square root of the count E[1/(1-cos theta)] - 2 of the vacuum density psi_0^2, and find the constant as a function of the accuracy.
results.label: op:registers

results.name: Monotonicity of the Thorin atoms of the one plaquette vacuum
results.summary: Open whether each Thorin atom of the one plaquette vacuum decreases monotonically toward one as the coupling goes to zero.
results.statement: Let psi_0 be the ground state of the one SU(2) plaquette Hamiltonian H_lambda = -lambda Delta + (1/lambda)(1 - cos theta) on class functions (Delta the Laplacian with eigenvalue -(n^2-1)/4 on the character chi_n), and let gamma_m(lambda) >= 1 be its Thorin atoms, so that psi_0(x) = psi_0(0) e^{ax} times the product over m of (1 + x/gamma_m) in x = cos(theta). The atoms decrease toward 1 as lambda tends to 0: the nearest is at 6.731, 1.206 and 1.0065 for lambda = 2, 1/2 and 1/10. Show that each gamma_m(lambda) is monotone in lambda.
results.label: op:vacuumthorin

results.name: Uniform gap for two dimensional SU(2) lattice Yang Mills from the coarsest lattice to the continuum
results.summary: In two dimensional SU(2) lattice Yang Mills on a cylinder the gap in physical units stays above an explicit positive multiple of the continuum gap at every lattice spacing, which gives a uniform Thorin gap inequality with constant one.
results.statement: Consider two dimensional SU(2) lattice Yang Mills theory with Wilson action on a cylinder whose spatial circle has $L$ sites and physical length $\ell$, so that the lattice spacing is $a=\ell/L$ and the Wilson coupling is $\beta=4/(g^2a^2)$. The transfer matrix is diagonal in characters with eigenvalues $u_n(\beta)^L$, where $u_n=I_n/I_1$ is a ratio of modified Bessel functions of the first kind, the lattice gap in physical units is $\Delta(a)=-\frac{L}{a}\log u_2(\beta)$, and the continuum gap is $\Delta_{\mathrm{cont}}=3g^2\ell/8$. Let $x=3g^2a^2/8$. For every lattice spacing, $\Delta(a)\ge\Delta_{\mathrm{cont}}\,\operatorname{arcsinh}(x)/x$. Consequently, for all $L\ge1$ and every gauge invariant observable, with nonnegative spectral measure $\mu^{(a)}$ in physical units and Thorin densities $T^{(a)}_\alpha(z)=\frac{1}{\pi y}\int\big(1-\cos(yE)\big)e^{-\alpha E}\,\mu^{(a)}(\mathrm dE)$ with $y=\sqrt{2z}$, the uniform Thorin gap inequality holds with constant one: $T^{(a)}_\alpha(z)\le e^{-\Delta_0(\alpha-\alpha')}\,T^{(a)}_{\alpha'}(z)$ for every lattice spacing $a$, every $z>0$ and all $\alpha\ge\alpha'>\alpha_0$, where $\alpha_0$ is such that $\int e^{-\alpha_0E}\,\mu^{(a)}(\mathrm dE)$ is finite, $\Delta_0=\Delta_{\mathrm{cont}}\,\operatorname{arcsinh}(x_\ell)/x_\ell$ and $x_\ell=\tfrac38 g^2\ell^2$.
results.label: thm:2dB

results.name: Riemann's kernel from the SU(2) sphere partition function
results.summary: Riemann's kernel for the xi function is a combination of the return density of Brownian motion on the three sphere and its time derivative, that is, of the two dimensional SU(2) Yang Mills partition function on the sphere and its area derivative.
results.statement: Let $F(A)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^2e^{-An^2/8}=e^{-A/8}Z_0(A)$, where $Z_0(A)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^2e^{-A(n^2-1)/8}$ is the partition function of two dimensional SU(2) Yang Mills theory on the sphere of area $A$. Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be Riemann's kernel. With $A=8\pi e^{2u}$, $\Phi(u)=-16\pi^2e^{9u/2}F'(A)-3\pi e^{5u/2}F(A)$.
results.label: prop:riemannB

results.name: Fisher zeros of the two dimensional sphere theory and the zeros of Xi
results.summary: Study the complex zeros in the area of the SU(2) sphere partition function and relate them to the zeros of the xi function through the identity with Riemann's kernel.
results.statement: Study the zeros of Z_0(A)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^2e^{-A(n^2-1)/8}, the partition function of two dimensional SU(2) Yang Mills theory on the sphere of area A, in the complex area plane (the Fisher zeros of the sphere theory), and relate them through the identity of Riemann's kernel with the sphere partition function to the zeros of the Riemann Xi function.
results.label: op:exact1

results.name: Route B Thorin densities across the Douglas Kazakov transition
results.summary: Follow the Thorin densities of the second route across the large N phase transition of two dimensional Yang Mills on the sphere, and ask for a number theoretic reading of the large N analogue of the identity with Riemann's kernel.
results.statement: The large N limit of two dimensional Yang Mills theory on the sphere has a third order phase transition at a critical area (Douglas and Kazakov). Track the Thorin densities of the second route (the transport of the spectral measure to a generalized gamma convolution) across the transition, and ask whether the analogue for SU(N) at large N of the identity of Riemann's kernel with the SU(2) sphere partition function has a number theoretic interpretation.
results.label: op:exact2

results.name: Positivity of character coefficients is preserved by a Migdal Kadanoff step
results.summary: One step of the Migdal Kadanoff recursion keeps all character coefficients of the plaquette weight nonnegative, so the four dimensional lattice theory with the plaquette weight of any rung is reflection positive.
results.statement: Let $f$ be a class function on SU(2) whose character coefficients are all nonnegative. Then the image of $f$ under one Migdal Kadanoff step (bond moving $f\mapsto f^{k}$ with $k=b^{d-2}$, normalised, followed by decimation, the $b^2$ fold convolution, which raises the character coefficients $u_n$ to the power $b^2$) has nonnegative character coefficients. The same holds for a general compact group.
results.label: lem:posB

results.name: Monotone likelihood ratio of the heat kernel makes the projected ladder map increasing
results.summary: If the SU(2) heat kernel has monotone likelihood ratio in time, which the book proves elsewhere, then the one dimensional heat kernel projected Migdal Kadanoff map is increasing.
results.statement: Let $R$ be the heat kernel projected Migdal Kadanoff map for SU(2) (start from the heat kernel law with coefficients $u_n=e^{-t(n^2-1)/4}$, $t=2/\beta$, apply one step with $b=2$ and $d=4$, read off the new second coefficient $u_2''=e^{-3t''/4}$ and set $R(\beta)=2/t''$). Suppose the SU(2) heat kernel $K_t(\theta)$ has monotone likelihood ratio in time, meaning that $\partial_\theta\log K_t(\theta)$ is increasing in $t$ for every $\theta\in(0,\pi)$. Then $R$ is increasing.
results.label: lem:mlrB

results.name: First passage criterion for the projected ladder
